title: "Versioned recipe library"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Versioned recipe library}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(dsOMOPClient)
```

The library provides 24 local, versioned starting points for analysis tables.
Each returns an ordinary language-2 recipe. Instantiation does not contact
sites, execute a query or collect patient rows. Existing capability and
publication checks apply when you explicitly execute the recipe.

```{r catalogue}
catalogue <- recipe_library_list()
catalogue[c("id", "template_version", "category", "output_names")]
recipe_library_list(query = "recorded")[c("id", "summary")]
```

An exact ID and version pin the installed definition. A NULL version selects
the installed recommendation. Required parameters have NULL defaults; that
means unbound, not a nullable clinical value. Use the description to inspect
parameters, contextual constraints, fixed policies, required inputs, schemas,
limitations, provenance and the complete constructor expansion.

```{r inspect}
description <- recipe_library_describe("demographics.baseline", "1.0.0")
description$parameters
description$constraints
description$expanded_template
```

Bind study definitions and then inspect the native plan. The selected visit
concept below is an example study input, not a universal clinical default.

```{r instantiate}
r <- recipe_library_instantiate("demographics.baseline", "1.0.0")
r <- recipe_bind(r, index = omop_event("visit_occurrence", 9201))
recipe_to_plan(r, version = 2L)
```

```{r execute, eval=FALSE}
recipe_execute(r, out = c(baseline = "analysis_baseline"),
               conns = conns, symbol = "omop")
```

The default index selection is first eligible, with unique observation
coverage and ambiguous/missing coverage dropped. Baseline windows end on day
-1. Annual age uses calendar years, and every template has episode grain.
Selection `all` can produce multiple rows per person. There is no implicit
requirement for a complete lookback unless the population explicitly declares
one. Review each entry's documentation before interpreting its table.

Numeric sources should have an explicit study scale and unit policy. Dense
measurement columns follow the finite declared concept set and vocabulary,
even at sites with no matching measurement rows. The source must be named
`measure`; other names are refused because carry-forward names that source.

```{r measurement}
panel <- recipe_library_instantiate("panel.measurements",
  index = omop_event("visit_occurrence", 9201),
  measure = omop_event("measurement", 3025315, value = "value_as_number",
    unit = omop_unit(9529), name = "measure"),
  horizon = 180L, bin_days = 30L)
recipe_to_plan(panel, version = 2L)
```

Coded social observations use concept-valued reducers and retain the native
concept presentation, including concept 0 and missing answers. They do not
infer highest attainment or an ordering of employment categories. Drug
adherence returns components; ratios require an explicit subsequent protected
mutation. Scores use their existing mappings through index and do not accept
a new lookback. New-user washout excludes starts in the lookback, not every
supply interval overlapping it. Matching is risk-set sampling; SCCS is a
partition table. Neither fits a causal model automatically.

Client metadata records the origin ID/version, definition checksum,
documentation revision and package version. JSON/YAML export/import preserves
it. The bound plan's semantic digest controls execution identity. Editing a
recipe creates a customised derivative; its library label does not certify
that it still equals the pinned definition.

```{r persistence}
json <- recipe_export_json(r)
restored <- recipe_import_json(json)
restored$meta$recipe_library
```

Use ordinary editing and `recipe_merge(..., prefix = ...)` to compose recipes.
Shared parameter definitions must agree. Prefixing preserves references but
can change plan digests and deterministic matched controls. Separate episode
rosters do not become joinable simply by merging them. The active-comparator
entry demonstrates private baseline/survival joins on a shared roster and
publishes only its two joined analysis tables.

Execution defaults to memory and small-site errors. Choose staging or skipping
explicitly; technical and schema errors cannot be skipped as small sites.
An absent optional source yields NA; an available event-free count source
normally yields zero. Only requested final roots undergo the existing support
checks. The library adds no thresholds, privacy budgets, server state, SQL,
wire fields or configuration.
